title: What If All the Sharks Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every shark vanished? A scallop fishery would be one of the first things to go.
We have a preview. Along the US East Coast, big sharks like hammerheads and tigers fell by over ninety-seven percent between 1970 and 2005.
Twelve species of rays, skates and small sharks increased. Cownose rays may now number up to forty million.
Those rays ate nearly all the adult bay scallops in the study area.
By 2004, North Carolina's century-old bay scallop fishery was finished.
Remove the top of the food chain and the effects ripple all the way down to the dinner plate.

description:
What if every shark vanished?
On the US East Coast, large sharks fell by more than 97 percent, rays boomed, and a century-old scallop fishery collapsed.
